proofPolicy.covered: Successful same-method own HTTP 200/201 with nonempty owned evidence; existing victim-only PostgreSQL target ID greater than each attacker-owned object; exact expected 403/404, unchanged real victim database for writes, and tested forged organizationId/employeeId/runId or equivalent victim selector. Never infer from invented IDs, 401, empty primary result, 429, 501, static reading or helper names. For session-derived own-employee endpoints with no caller-selectable employer or foreign resource ID, the route-specific alternative requires two independently successful own HTTP controls, the same signed-in account denied 403 after real DB membership revocation, and a separately seeded victim employer's PostgreSQL snapshot unchanged; do not report this as a foreign-ID attempt. On selector-based routes, actual victim IDs must be read back from real PG and exceed both persisted attacker-owned comparator IDs; >6 alone is inadequate. Static GET catalogs must be explicitly labeled tenant-gated metadata, while exports validate seeded owned content, response bytes and integrity hashes when available.
